memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "There the Lord will give you an anxious mind, eyes weary with longing, and a despairing heart. You will live in constant suspense, filled with dread both night and day, never sure of your life. In the morning you will say, 'If only it were evening!' and in the evening, 'If only it were morning!' — because of the terror that will fill your hearts... The Lord will send you back in ships to Egypt... There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you." — Deut 28:66-68 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends at the lowest possible point: a life of constant dread, an anxious mind, a despairing heart, never sure of tomorrow, longing for morning at night and evening in the morning. And finally, a return to Egypt — back to the very slavery God had rescued them from — with no one even willing to buy them. It is the picture of a redemption undone, a people who forsook God ending up back in bondage. The chapter closes in darkness.

But we do not close our devotion in darkness, because Deuteronomy 28 is not the last word. It shows us where the road of forsaking God ends — in dread, restlessness, and slavery. And it makes us ache for a Redeemer who could reverse it all.

That Redeemer came. Where this chapter ends with a return to slavery, Jesus came to set captives free (Luke 4:18). Where it describes a heart filled with dread day and night, Christ gives a peace the world cannot give (John 14:27). Where it ends with a redemption undone, the cross accomplishes a redemption that can never be undone.

This is why the whole chapter, blessing and curse alike, ultimately points to Christ. He took the curse (Gal 3:13) so we could have the blessing. He entered the darkness so we could walk in light. If you belong to Him, the last word over your life is not dread but hope, not slavery but freedom, not Egypt but home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live in the freedom and peace Christ won, or in anxious dread?
2. How does the ending of this chapter deepen my gratitude for the gospel?
3. What "Egypt" of bondage has Christ set me free from?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You reverse the curse. Where sin leads to dread and slavery, You give peace and freedom. Thank You that in You my last word is hope, not despair. Amen.
